title: PARK THE MEMORY FOR SUPPORTED CARE
goal: Stop reopening the memory and move it toward supported care.
steps:
1. Stop Memory Detail — Stop adding sensory detail or searching for meaning.
2. Name Later Container — Choose a qualified professional or safe appointment for later support.
3. Name One Reminder — Say one short reminder that the topic needs supported care.
4. Close The Topic — End the reminder without reopening the memory.
5. Return Externally — Return attention to a neutral task in the current environment.
win: The topic was parked for qualified support and attention settled on a neutral task in the present.
supports:
• Use familiar surroundings; name the place.
• Stop if you feel less present; contact someone you trust.
• Hold something familiar; keep lighting comfortable.
• Orient to today's date and place; choose gentle, ordinary movement.
• Stop if less present; keep the room comfortably lit.
formula_flow: Stop Memory Detail → Name Later Container → Name One Reminder → Close The Topic → Return Externally
safety:
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open. Use only present-day room, date, place and support orientation. Do not revisit memories in detail, use trauma imagery, intensify sensations, or attempt unsupervised processing. Stop for flooding, dissociation, or weakened orientation and connect with qualified human support.
This is stabilisation only, not trauma treatment.

title: BUILD A PRESENT-DAY SAFETY MAP
goal: Build a short present-day safety map you can actually use.
steps:
1. Name Current Supports — Name two present-day supports that can actually be reached.
2. Mark Safe Places — Name one familiar place where you feel more present and steady.
3. Name Exit Options — Identify a practical exit from the current stressful setting.
4. Choose One Contact — Choose the person or service to contact if steadiness drops.
5. Hold Map in Mind — Keep the short map in mind and avoid adding memory content.
win: You could name reachable support, a steadier place, an exit, and who to contact if needed.

• Keep lighting comfortable; contact someone you trust.
• Stop if you feel less present; choose gentle, ordinary movement.
• Move gently; feel your feet on the floor.

title: ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH
goal: Use one light label, then return immediately to the raw experience.
steps:
1. Apply Quiet — As events arise, apply a quiet category: hearing, planning, heat, remembering, pressure.
2. Use Word — Use one word once, then return to the raw event.
3. Name Lightly — If a label starts producing analysis, name that ‘explaining’ and release it.
win: A single word named the event without turning into an explanation about it.
supports:
• Delay the verdict; ask what would change your mind.
• Ask what would disprove it; add the missing context.
• Avoid treating guesses as facts; check what you actually know.
• Check another angle; delay major conclusions when upset.
• Check the base rate; use current facts.
formula_flow: Apply Quiet → Use Word → Name Lightly
safety:
PAUSE
Drop noting if labels become compulsive, critical, or distancing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
goal: Shorten the delay between noticing distraction and returning to the anchor.
steps:
1. Choose Precise — Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks.
2. Return Instead — Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
3. Track Interval — Track the interval between noticing and reconnection.
4. Let Practice — Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.
win: The gap from 'I wandered' to reconnection became visibly smaller during the practice.
supports:
• Use one screen; return after interruptions.
• Mute alerts; reduce background noise.
• Use a short focus block; clear visual clutter.
• Take a real screen break; reduce nearby noise.
• Keep one task visible; close extra tabs.
formula_flow: Choose Precise → Return Instead → Track Interval → Let Practice
safety:
PAUSE
Release focus if effort becomes rigid, painful, or compulsive.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE ACTION HAD MANY AUTHORS
goal: Share authorship of an action with the conditions that also helped cause it.
steps:
1. Name Conditions — Review one action and name its conditions: intention, habit, body capacity, other people, resources, timing, culture, and chance.
2. Place Yourself — Place yourself among these causes rather than above them.
3. Keep Responsibility — Keep responsibility for your contribution while releasing sole authorship.
win: Your contribution remained accountable while habit, capacity, timing, people, culture, and chance re-entered the picture.
supports:
• Check the facts separately; separate feeling from fact.
• Lower nearby noise; notice what changed physically.
• Eat, drink, or rest if needed; let intensity fall.
• Notice body tension; rest before deciding.
• Give the feeling time to move; wait before sending messages.
formula_flow: Name Conditions → Place Yourself → Keep Responsibility
safety:
PAUSE
Do not scattered accountability for choices that caused harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
goal: Make an intentionally imperfect start, repair one useful part, and stop polishing.
steps:
1. Throwaway — Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Make Wrong — Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, rough mental outline, or unfinished opening.
3. Fix One — Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Continue Clean — Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.
win: The rough beginning became editable after exactly one correction instead of needing to become impressive.
supports:
• Limit checking passes; use actual requirements.
• Define good enough first; stop low-value changes.
• Make rough version; leave minor flaws.
• Separate errors from polish; limit checking.
• Ship useful work; set finish time.
formula_flow: Throwaway → Make Wrong → Fix One → Continue Clean
safety:
PAUSE
Never use deliberate errors in medical, legal, financial, safety-critical, submitted, or live shared work.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
goal: Test whether a thought actually clarifies, protects, and leaves you more capable.
steps:
1. Ask Thought — Ask the current thought three questions: Does it clarify the next move.
2. Check Protection — Does it protect something real.
3. Leave Me — Does it leave me more capable afterward.
4. Score Yes — Score each yes or no.
5. Thank Warning — If it fails two, thank the warning and appoint a different inner adviser.
win: A thought that failed most of the test lost its advisory role without needing to be argued out of existence.
supports:
• Shrink the first action; reward starting, not finishing.
• Choose a rough beginning; start before you feel ready.
• Open only what you need; remove one barrier.
• Lower standards briefly; stop planning after one action.
• Prepare first; open the task.
formula_flow: Ask Thought → Check Protection → Leave Me → Score Yes → Thank Warning
safety:
PAUSE
A harsh message may still contain facts; extract them before dismissal.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SOFT DELIVERY, SOLID MESSAGE
goal: Keep the message firm while removing unnecessary attack from its delivery.
steps:
1. Remove Attacks — Remove attacks from your wording.
2. Validate Understandable — Show one sign of genuine interest, validate the understandable part of the other experience, and use an easy rather than contemptuous manner.
3. Keep Core — Keep your core message unchanged.
4. Edit Delivery — Gentleness edits delivery, not truth.
win: Interest, validation, and an easier manner changed the tone without changing the core truth.
supports:
• Keep one issue per conversation; separate facts from tone.
• Say the main point first; clarify the deadline.
• Check the agreed deadline; lead with the point.
• Separate tone from facts; use one example.
• Name the desired change; ask for a specific next action.

safety:
PAUSE
Do not prioritise pleasantness over protection in abusive dynamics.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SELF-RESPECT CHECKSUM
goal: Protect self-respect by checking fairness, truth, values, and unnecessary apology before speaking.
steps:
1. Respond Verify — Before responding, verify four conditions: fair to both sides; no apology for merely existing or setting a limit; aligned with your values; completely truthful.
2. Revise Sentence — Revise any sentence that fails the checksum.
3. Speak Cleanly — Then speak without extra justification.
win: The final response passed all four conditions and did not need extra justification afterward.
supports:
• Choose one value-led action; use one priority.
• Remove one conflict; use values to choose trade-offs.
• Keep the action small; name today's value.
• Accept the trade-off; protect important time.
• Remove one conflicting commitment; make the next hour reflect it.
formula_flow: Respond Verify → Revise Sentence → Speak Cleanly
safety:
PAUSE
Fairness does not require equal power where harm or coercion exists.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FOUR-PART LIMIT
goal: Make a boundary specific enough that your own next action is clear.
steps:
1. State Triggering — State the triggering condition, your limit, the action you will take, and when you will take it.
2. Remove Threats — Remove threats that depend on the other person changing.
3. Practise Line — Practise the line once at speaking volume, then prepare the consequence before delivery.
win: Condition, limit, consequence, and timing were stated without relying on the other person to obey.
supports:
• Protect your capacity; use a short no.
• Notice resentment as a warning; keep consequences realistic.
• Repeat the same wording calmly; let guilt pass.
• Use one clear sentence; do not debate your limit.
• Notice resentment early; keep the limit simple.

PAUSE

goal: Offer the compassionate action that is yours without taking over someone else's emotional work.

• Protect your capacity; keep consequences realistic.
• Delay your answer; notice resentment as a warning.
• Do not debate your limit; take time before saying yes.

title: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
goal: Say the unsent truth in your mind, then leave contact alone for a full day.
steps:
1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you.
2. Say What Happened — In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Do Not Edit — Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Wait — Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.
win: The message expressed what happened, felt, mattered, and could be released without becoming an immediate send.
supports:
• Notice the first automatic moment; move the cue.
• Interrupt the sequence; notice the trigger.
• Interrupt the usual sequence; expect slips and restart quickly.
• Reduce easy access to triggers; reset after slips.
• Keep replacement easy; change the environment first.

title: CROSS OUT THE EXPIRED FUTURE
goal: Retire a prediction the moment the condition that made it relevant has ended.
steps:
1. Picture Prediction — Picture the prediction and the exact condition that makes it obsolete: date passed, result known, action completed, evidence changed.
2. Imagine Line — When that condition arrives, imagine a line through the prediction and picture the word EXPIRED.
3. Remove Vote — It may remain historically visible, but it receives no further vote.
win: The forecast was mentally stamped expired and stopped influencing present choices once its deadline or evidence changed.
supports:
• Check the base rate; use a real example.
• Notice absolute words like always; avoid treating guesses as facts.
• Check the whole situation; look for one missing fact.
• Delay the verdict; check what you actually know.
• Use current facts; question absolute words.
formula_flow: Picture Prediction → Imagine Line → Remove Vote
safety:
PAUSE
Reopen only when genuinely new evidence creates a new forecast.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN ANTICIPATION INTO INVENTORY
goal: Convert repeated future scenes into preparation until they stop producing anything new.
steps:
1. Repeat Extract — Each time the same future scene repeats, extract one actionable item: question, document, rehearsal, route, support, or if-then link.
2. Add Checklist — Add it to a checklist.
3. Stamp Simulation — When repetition yields no new preparation, stamp the simulation PAID IN FULL and switch to execution.
win: Each useful replay became a checklist item, and repetition was closed once no new preparation emerged.
supports:
• Avoid repeated pulse checking; loosen your shoulders.
• Use ordinary surroundings; seek care for new severe symptoms.
• Keep your body supported; look at ordinary objects nearby.
• Stay somewhere physically safe; wait out the surge.
• Unclench your jaw and shoulders; keep movements gentle.

2. Small — What small feature would suddenly matter—someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, morning light.
3. Choose Behaviour — Choose one behaviour that honours that recovered value today, without romanticising real hardship.

WIN
A small feature of life became newly valuable and one behaviour honoured it without denying real hardship.

• Notice body tension; check basic needs.
• Notice what changed physically; do one steadying action.
• Give the feeling time to move; slow physical pace.
• Check the facts separately; avoid decisions at peak emotion.
• Name the emotion; use plain language.

MIND BEND
Familiarity hides value by making access feel guaranteed — imagined absence can reveal what ordinary presence had made invisible.

FORMULA FLOW
Picture → Small → Choose Behaviour

SAFETY
PAUSE
Avoid loss imagery if it worsens grief, trauma, or suicidal thinking.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
goal: Replace inflammatory language with the exact frequency, loss, or behaviour it refers to.
steps:
1. Spot Absolutes — Catch any absolute or inflammatory word in your account.
2. Cool The Words — Replace each one with a precise fact: ‘always’ becomes the actual frequency; ‘destroyed’ becomes the specific loss; ‘evil’ becomes the observed behaviour.
3. Read Action — Say the cooler version once and notice what action it supports.
win: The cooler account kept the facts and produced a more specific next action.
supports:
• Stay somewhere physically safe; unclench your jaw.
• Unclench your jaw and shoulders; sit somewhere safe.
• Loosen your shoulders; seek care for new severe symptoms.
• Reduce caffeine; use ordinary surroundings.
• Give the surge time to pass; stop body scanning.
formula_flow: Spot Absolutes → Cool The Words → Read Action
safety:
PAUSE
Retain strong moral language when accurate naming is necessary.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LOOK FOR THE MISSING DANGER
goal: Look once for the sign that should be present if the feared model is right.
steps:
1. Ask Sign — Ask what sign must exist right now if the feared model is correct.
2. Search Fairly — Search once, fairly.
3. Mark Absence — If it is absent, keep that absence and reduce—not erase—the model’s weight.
4. Name Explanation — Name the alternate explanation strengthened by the missing sign.
win: The required danger sign was either found or honestly absent, and the model's weight changed accordingly.
supports:
• Reset after slips; interrupt the sequence.
• Remove easy access; notice the first automatic moment.
• Delay the routine; reduce easy access to triggers.
• Interrupt the usual sequence; use the same replacement repeatedly.
• Expect slips and restart quickly; make the old habit harder.

safety:
PAUSE
Never use absent evidence to dismiss subtle or delayed safety risks.

title: THREE ACTIVE FUTURES ONLY
goal: Keep only three future predictions active enough to influence the decision.
steps:
1. Picture Predictions — Picture the three predictions currently most relevant.
2. Enter Retiring — Any new prediction may enter only by retiring one, merging with one, or proving more useful for the decision.
3. Retire One — Mentally remove any retired prediction from view.
4. Act Portfolio — Act from the remaining three rather than unlimited mental possibilities.
win: Every extra forecast had to replace, merge with, or outperform one already on the mental board.
supports:
• Make the old habit harder; add small friction.
• Keep replacement easy; replace one response.
• Change the environment first; make the new habit easier.
• Change the environment; interrupt the usual sequence.
• Reset without self-criticism; interrupt the sequence.

safety:

title: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
goal: Give a truly finished topic one repeatable sensory ending and a clear return time.
steps:
1. Choose A Finish — Choose one finish you can repeat: wash your hands, hear a soft sound, touch a doorframe, or change the light.
2. Pair It — Pair it with one short answer in your mind and a time to think about it again.
3. Close It — Use the sensory finish only when the topic is truly closed.
win: The subject closed with a physical cue, one short mental answer, and a defined point for any future review.
supports:
• Name three visible objects; track one texture.
• Name today's date; notice temperature and texture.
• Keep eyes open; slow your physical pace.
• Feel both feet; touch a stable surface.
• Reduce sensory input if needed; notice three colours.

PAUSE
Do not close matters that still require urgent action.

title: MEASURE THE EMOTION’S VELOCITY
goal: Track whether an emotion is rising, steady, or falling before acting from its intensity.
steps:
1. Set Level — At three intervals, keep not only level but direction and speed: rising fast, steady, falling slowly.
2. Add Action — Add the action impulse at each point.
3. Make Decisions — Make decisions from trajectory plus facts, not from the first intensity number alone.
win: Three readings showed level, direction, speed, and action urge, so the decision used the whole trajectory.
supports:
• Make access harder; use your hands.
• Tell someone if the urge spikes; change rooms if possible.
• Keep your hands busy; remember urges peak and fall.
• Change locations; avoid bargaining.
• Avoid bargaining with the urge; delay ten minutes.

safety:
PAUSE
Escalating risk calls for support before further tracking.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN EACH LOAD TO ITS SOURCE
goal: Give each source of stress only the share of body alarm it actually contributed.
steps:
1. Estimate Contribution — Name current stressors and estimate each contribution to body alarm.
2. Imagine Arrows — Imagine arrows from the present feeling back to its actual sources.
3. Stop Blaming — Address the largest actionable contributor first; stop blaming the most visible issue for unrelated load.
win: The largest actionable source became clearer, and the most visible problem stopped carrying unrelated load.
supports:
• Seek care for new severe symptoms; unclench your jaw.
• Reduce caffeine; let breathing stay natural.
• Wait out the surge; use ordinary surroundings.
• Sip water if it helps; avoid repeated pulse checking.
• Look at ordinary objects nearby; keep your body supported.

title: GLOBAL LABELS NEED THREE RECEIPTS
goal: Test a global identity label against recent evidence that both supports and complicates it.
steps:
1. Name Appears — When a global label appears, name three recent behaviours that support it and three that complicate it.
2. Replace Identity — If the evidence is mixed, replace identity with a narrower situational description.
win: Six behaviours made the label narrower, or showed that a situational description fit better.
supports:
• Add the missing context; question absolute words.
• Use recent, concrete evidence; look for one missing fact.
• Ask what else could fit; avoid treating guesses as facts.
• Separate guess from evidence; check what you actually know.
• Check another angle; notice absolute words like always.
formula_flow: Name Appears → Replace Identity
safety:
PAUSE
Do not turn the audit into exhaustive self-surveillance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

• Move the cue; remove easy access.
• Keep replacement easy; notice the trigger.

title: THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE
goal: Restore what came after the painful ending instead of letting memory stop at the worst frame.
steps:
1. End Retell — Retell only enough to reach the painful ending.
2. Follow Escape — Then append what actually followed: escape, help, adaptation, learning, regained ability, or today’s status.
3. Don't Invent — Do not invent redemption.
4. Restore — Restore the omitted chronology.
win: The chronology continued into real help, adaptation, learning, regained ability, or today's status without invented redemption.
supports:
• Reduce easy access to triggers; change one cue.
• Notice the first automatic moment; use the same replacement repeatedly.
• Reset after slips; keep replacement easy.
• Notice the trigger; make the new habit easier.
• Change the environment; interrupt the sequence.

safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SAY THE SENTENCE HISTORY NEVER RECEIVED
goal: Say the words the past never received while making clear that today cannot rewrite then.
steps:
1. Picture Words — Picture the exact words you could not say or hear.
2. Speak Empty — Say them quietly in your mind or to an empty room while clearly stating that this is present-day completion, not a changed past.
3. Add Response — Add the response current-you can now provide.
win: The missing sentence was expressed and current-you supplied a response without pretending history had changed.
supports:
• Lower the first demand; begin with the easiest part.
• Begin while unsure; remove one barrier.
• Choose tiny action; set a two-minute timer.
• Start before you feel ready; lower standards briefly.
• Skip extra setup; use one window.
formula_flow: Picture Words → Speak Empty → Add Response
safety:
PAUSE
Do not contact unsafe people or mistake imagined response for evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
goal: Measure who carries the hidden work of the relationship across a defined period.
steps:
1. Plan Carries — Across a defined period, tally who initiates, accommodates, repairs, plans, and carries emotional follow-up.
2. Add Context — Include background for genuine capacity differences.
3. Use Categories — Discuss the pattern using categories, not accusations, and request one clear rebalance.
win: Initiation, accommodation, repair, planning, and follow-up became categories that could support one concrete rebalance request.
supports:
• Avoid treating guesses as facts; test the assumption.
• Ask what would change your mind; delay the verdict.
• Use recent, concrete evidence; notice absolute words like always.
• Separate possibility from probability; ask what else could fit.
• Check another angle; look for one missing fact.
formula_flow: Plan Carries → Add Context → Use Categories
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use the map to demand identical contributions under unequal circumstances.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
goal: Prefer the option whose failure becomes visible while correction is still practical.
steps:
1. Name Options — Name the two or three live options. For each, picture the specific way it could fail—not a vague fear.
2. Name Failure — Name the earliest visible sign that failure has begun. It must be visible or clear, not a feeling alone.
3. Warning — State what corrective action would still be available when that sign appears and what cost has already accumulated.
4. Choose Visible — Choose the option whose reliable warning arrives while correction is still practical. Use this as one decision criterion, not the whole verdict.
win: Each option had a specific failure sign, remaining correction, and accumulated cost before one warning system was favoured.
supports:
• Delay the message; lower stimulation for a minute.
• Do one steadying action; name the emotion.
• Wait before sending messages; use simple words for the problem.
• Lower nearby noise; use plain language.
• Rest before deciding; notice what changed physically.
formula_flow: Name Options → Name Failure → Warning → Choose Visible
safety:
PAUSE
For high-stakes, irreversible, medical, legal, financial, or safety decisions, use qualified advice and all required criteria.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND THE MOMENT THE FLOOR CATCHES YOU
goal: Feel the exact instant the floor takes your weight during slow shifts.
steps:
1. Shift Weight — Stand safely and shift weight slowly left, centre, right, then forward and back.
2. Identify Instant — At each transition, spot the exact instant the receiving foot supports you.
3. Finish Centre — Finish at centre and name the strongest contact point.
win: Each transition revealed a receiving foot, and the practice ended on the strongest central contact point.
supports:
• Let breaths happen; unclench your jaw.
• Keep your body supported; reduce caffeine.
• Unclench your jaw and shoulders; reduce extra stimulation.
• Keep movements gentle; look at ordinary objects nearby.
• Stop body scanning; seek care for new severe symptoms.

safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

45–60 seconds

GOAL
Feel the exact instant the floor takes your weight during slow shifts.

HOW TO PLAY
1. Shift Weight — Stand safely and shift weight slowly left, centre, right, then forward and back.
2. Identify Instant — At each transition, spot the exact instant the receiving foot supports you.
3. Finish Centre — Finish at centre and name the strongest contact point.

WIN
Each transition revealed a receiving foot, and the practice ended on the strongest central contact point.

• Let breaths happen; unclench your jaw.
• Keep your body supported; reduce caffeine.
• Unclench your jaw and shoulders; reduce extra stimulation.
• Keep movements gentle; look at ordinary objects nearby.
• Stop body scanning; seek care for new severe symptoms.

MIND BEND

Shift Weight → Identify Instant → Finish Centre

PAUSE
Practise seated or with assistance if balance is uncertain.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
goal: Use near, middle, and far sounds to reopen the sense of space around you.
steps:
1. Identify Nearest — Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.
2. Move Attention — Move attention outward through those distances, then back once.
3. Let Far — Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one.
win: Attention travelled outward and back once, and the farthest sound made the nearest layer feel less enclosing.
supports:
• Keep new facts separate; stop researching after enough evidence.
• Set a decision deadline; avoid reopening without new facts.
• Ignore imagined regret; limit the options.
• Choose the option you can support; name the non-negotiables.
• Stop extra research; choose by the strongest evidence.
formula_flow: Identify Nearest → Move Attention → Let Far
safety:
PAUSE
Use hearing protection rather than attention practice in unsafe noise.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND THE SENSE FACT THE STORY CANNOT EXPLAIN
goal: Find one sensory fact the feared story should not be able to explain away.
steps:
1. State Fear — State the feared scenario.
2. Search Sensory — Search for one sensory fact opposite with it: an unlocked exit, ordinary background conversation, relaxed posture nearby, intact support, current silence.
3. Predict Fact — Explain in one line why the model fails to predict that fact.
win: A real exit, ordinary sound, relaxed posture, intact support, or silence contradicted one prediction of the threat model.
supports:
• Separate possibility from probability; delay major conclusions when upset.
• Ask what would disprove it; check another angle.
• Avoid treating guesses as facts; look for one missing fact.
• Notice absolute words like always; add the missing context.
• Use current facts; test the assumption.
formula_flow: State Fear → Search Sensory → Predict Fact
safety:
PAUSE
Never let one neutral cue overrule concrete evidence of danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

2. Search Sensory — Search for one sensory fact opposite with it: an unlocked exit, ordinary background conversation, relaxed posture nearby, intact support, current silence.
3. Predict Fact — Explain in one line why the model fails to predict that fact.

WIN
A real exit, ordinary sound, relaxed posture, intact support, or silence contradicted one prediction of the threat model.

• Separate possibility from probability; delay major conclusions when upset.
• Ask what would disprove it; check another angle.
• Avoid treating guesses as facts; look for one missing fact.
• Notice absolute words like always; add the missing context.
• Use current facts; test the assumption.

MIND BEND
A story weakens when it fails to predict something currently visible — disconfirming detail matters because good models must explain the whole scene.

FORMULA FLOW
State Fear → Search Sensory → Predict Fact

SAFETY
PAUSE
Never let one neutral cue overrule concrete evidence of danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLOSE THE INPUT VALVE
goal: Stop nonessential input long enough to hear what your own mind already contains.
steps:
1. Choose Defined — Choose a defined period with no nonessential news, feeds, podcasts, searches, or advice.

win: The feed went quiet for a defined period, revealing which memories, conclusions, or next actions emerged without fresh stimulation.
supports:

• Return to one target; clear visual clutter.
• Put the phone out of reach; choose one target.
• Keep one task visible; use one window at a time.
• Protect one focus block; take a short break.

title: WHEN DOES THIS INFORMATION EXPIRE?
goal: Mark old information as expired instead of letting it keep voting in the current decision.
steps:
1. Picture Expiry — For each influential input, picture an expiry condition: price changes, role ends, policy updates, health status shifts, deadline passes.
2. Expire Old Data — Notice any expired item. Stop letting it guide new behaviour until the information is refreshed.
win: At least one influential input received an expiry condition and stopped guiding behaviour once it was stale.
supports:
• Mute alerts; park secondary tasks.
• Close extra tabs; reduce nearby noise.
• Return after interruptions; use a short focus block.
• Take a real screen break; return to one target.
• Close what you do not need; use one screen.

title: WHAT KIND OF EFFORT IS THIS?
goal: Identify what kind of effort you are feeling before deciding that effort means failure.
steps:
1. Use Evidence — Classify the strain using evidence.
2. Stop Novelty — If danger, stop; if novelty, allow learning; if skill growth, dose it; if poor design, simplify the system.
3. Respond Category — Respond to the category instead of interpreting all effort as failure.
win: Danger, novelty, skill growth, or poor design each received a different response instead of one global verdict.
supports:
• Add small friction; change the environment.
• Move the cue; notice the trigger.
• Reset without self-criticism; delay the routine.
• Replace one response; make the new habit easier.
• Change the environment first; keep replacement easy.

title: SWAP OUTCOME CONTROL FOR PROCESS CONTROL
goal: Score yourself on a process you control instead of an outcome you can only influence.
steps:
1. Name Desired — Name the desired outcome and cross it out as the score.
2. Practise Applications — Substitute one visible process variable fully under your control—calls made, honest minutes practised, applications sent, boundary delivered.
3. Score the Process — Check success only on that variable for the chosen period.
win: Success became calls made, honest minutes, applications, or a delivered boundary rather than the final result.
supports:
• Use a decision deadline; choose good enough.
• Use a deadline; avoid reopening settled choices.
• Limit checking; leave one question unanswered.
• Name what is unknown; stop reopening choices.
• Accept a small margin of risk; choose a good-enough option.

title: THREE INCOMPATIBLE READINGS
goal: Hold three rival stories open and let later evidence decide which one survives.
steps:
1. Hold Cue — Keep the same cue in mind: a delayed reply, expression, or result.
2. Identify Future — Generate three explanations that cannot all be true and identify what future evidence would separate them.
3. Receive Support — Delay commitment until one explanation receives support.
win: The same cue supported multiple readings and commitment was delayed until one gained actual support.
supports:
• Name what is unknown; set a limit on checking.
• Use a decision deadline; name what is known.
• Ask what is controllable now; notice when checking stops helping.
• Act with uncertainty; stop reopening choices.
• Delay reassurance; limit checking.

safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LEAVE ONE THING BETTER
goal: Improve one small part of the world without using the contribution to prove your worth.
steps:
1. Choose Target — Choose a person, place, system, or situation you can improve slightly.
2. Pick Contribution — Name one small useful contribution.
3. Do It — Complete the contribution without using it to prove your worth.
win: A person, place, system, or situation became slightly better and the act did not need to become self-evidence.
supports:
• Check the whole situation; delay major conclusions when upset.
• Check another angle; avoid treating guesses as facts.
• Look for one missing fact; separate possibility from probability.
• Delay the verdict; ask what would disprove it.
• Test the assumption; use recent, concrete evidence.

title: WHAT MATERIAL CONSEQUENCE DOES STATUS ACTUALLY HAVE?

• Use your own timeline; track progress by your values.
• Return to your own baseline; notice hidden differences.

title: LEAVE COMPARISON AT THE DOOR
goal: Keep comparison outside the performance and count the commitment you actually kept.

title: ALARM, NOT VERDICT
goal: Lower the panic load without testing your heart sensations or forcing your breathing.
steps:
1. See Room — Keep your eyes open and name three edges or corners you can see.
2. Slow One Move — Slow one visible movement—your hands, feet, or walking pace—without forcing your breathing.
3. Call Support — Tell a safe person, “I’m having a panic surge. Stay with me for a minute.”
win: Your attention widened to the room, one movement slowed, and a safe person was brought into the moment.
supports:
• Let breaths happen; seek care for new severe symptoms.
• Avoid symptom searching; sit somewhere safe.
• Sip water if it helps; use ordinary surroundings.
• Let breathing stay natural; wait out the surge.
• Stop body scanning; reduce extra stimulation.
formula_flow: See Room → Slow One Move → Call Support
safety:
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open and orient to the room. Stop if symptoms intensify, you feel faint, or a medical problem may be possible. Call Triple Zero (000) for an emergency; otherwise use qualified medical advice. Do not induce or test symptoms.
This is brief self-help, not diagnosis or treatment.

title: LEAVE THE HAZARD ZONE
play_time: ACT NOW — MOVE TO LIVE SUPPORT
goal: Leave immediate hazards and let another person help slow a level of activation you cannot safely manage alone.
steps:
1. Exit Risk Area — Step away from traffic, heights, weapons, substances, or conflict.
2. Lower Outside Stimulation — Choose a quieter known place without driving yourself there.
3. Tell Safe Human — Tell someone clearly that you cannot slow down safely.
4. Contact Urgent Help — Use emergency or crisis support from the Safety section.
5. Wait With Support — Remain with support until the activation is professionally assessed.
win: You reached a lower-risk setting and remained with support until professional assessment began.
supports:
• Move to a quieter place.
• Keep a trusted person with you.
• Avoid driving or risky decisions.
• Reduce caffeine and other stimulants.
• Get professional support now.
formula_flow: Exit Risk Area → Lower Outside Stimulation → Tell Safe Human → Contact Urgent Help → Wait With Support
safety:
PAUSE
IMMEDIATE DANGER OR POSSIBLE MEDICAL EMERGENCY: call Triple Zero (000) now.
24/7 CRISIS SUPPORT: call Lifeline 13 11 14 or text 0477 13 11 14.
Stay with a safe person and follow qualified support. Do not return to ordinary rituals.

t:
LEAVE THE HAZARD ZONE

PLAY TIME
ACT NOW — MOVE TO LIVE SUPPORT

GOAL
Leave immediate hazards and let another person help slow a level of activation you cannot safely manage alone.

HOW TO PLAY
1. Exit Risk Area — Step away from traffic, heights, weapons, substances, or conflict.
2. Lower Outside Stimulation — Choose a quieter known place without driving yourself there.
3. Tell Safe Human — Tell someone clearly that you cannot slow down safely.
4. Contact Urgent Help — Use emergency or crisis support from the Safety section.
5. Wait With Support — Remain with support until the activation is professionally assessed.

WIN
You reached a lower-risk setting and remained with support until professional assessment began.

• Move to a quieter place.
• Keep a trusted person with you.
• Avoid driving or risky decisions.
• Reduce caffeine and other stimulants.
• Get professional support now.

MIND BEND
When activation outruns judgement, reducing hazards matters more than understanding the state. Environment can carry safety while the nervous system cannot.

title: NO SECRET MESSAGE
goal: Let an intrusive thought exist without treating its arrival as a message.
steps:
1. Name Arrival — Say, “A thought showed up.”
2. Remove Message — Add, “Showing up is not a message.”
3. Pick Ordinary — Name one ordinary thing in front of you that has nothing to do with the thought.
4. Continue Ten — Do that ordinary thing for ten seconds without checking whether the thought is gone.
win: The thought stayed unanswered while attention moved into an ordinary object and action unrelated to it.
supports:
• Avoid testing what it means; return to the current task.
• Notice mental content; do not seek repeated reassurance.
• Notice it as mental content; allow uncertainty.
• Do not argue with the thought; return to the task.
• Let uncertainty remain; avoid confessing for relief.
formula_flow: Name Arrival → Remove Message → Pick Ordinary → Continue Ten
safety:
PAUSE
